summary: Single pre-declared confirmatory run of preregistration_v5.json (sha 6222b79d...2b1e1, unchanged) on the frozen 1,225-file bars1d_2004_2013 panel, labelled "confirmatory, unseen, partial universe (1,225 names)". Engine functions copied verbatim from EXEC_v5_engine.py; no threshold or definition changed. Result: every trading cell is NEGATIVE on 2004-2013. V5-1 (E1, n=205) -0.38% [-0.66, -0.09]; V5-2 (E2, n=1,243) -0.21% [-0.38, -0.01]; V5-3 (E1|B1 ON, n=42) -0.72% [-1.29, -0.24]; V5-4 (E2|B1 ON, n=258) -0.24% [-0.53, +0.08]; V5-5 (E1|B2 ON, n=88) -0.54% [-0.96, -0.12]. Holm-adjusted p = 1.000 for all five; quarters positive 8-24%; C1 excess <= 0 for both base cells (-0.25 / -0.06); B1 ON share only 18.4% of days and ON-OFF differences are negative (-0.43 E1, -0.03 E2); B2 ON-OFF -0.27, Spearman rho 0.01. Both confirmatory halves negative for every cell. Kill rule K1 (regime artefact) fires: C1 excess <= 0 for both V5-1 and V5-2 AND the best cell's 2004-2008 half (-0.26%) < -0.20%. K2 (mirror +0.03 n.s.), K3 (placebo <= 0), K4 (>= $500M tier is the only positive slice for V5-2) do not fire. Decision computed in code: RED. The one-day B1 window shift flagged by the verifier changes n by +-3 and moves every gated statistic slightly further negative; no verdict changes. V5-6 ladder pooled -0.30 [-0.43, -0.17] (research fail); V5-7a >= 25% movers -1.48 vs 8-25% -0.22 (expectation not met). Per-capital K=5 loses money in 9 of 10 years for every cell (V5-2 at 20% each: -46.8% total). The 2004-2013 window is now SEEN (things_tried.csv, 11 rows appended). Reading: 2004-2013 resembles 2015-2019 (effect absent, sign negative), not 2020-2024; the seen-window edge and its B1 gate do not generalise, and this is on the universe most biased in the rule's favour.
decision_rationale: Decision tree computed in code with precedence RED > AMBER > GREEN (stricter reading where clauses overlap). (1) Kill rule K1 fires on the confirmatory window: confirmatory excess over C1 is <= 0 for BOTH base cells (V5-1 -0.25% [-0.56, ...], V5-2 -0.06% [-0.22, ...]) and the best family cell by mean (V5-2) has a confirmatory half below -0.20% (2004-2008: -0.26%; 2009-2013: -0.17%). (2) Independently of K1, no gated cell meets the registered gates and none is AMBER-eligible: V5-3 fails 12 of 15 gates (lower CI -1.29, ON-OFF -0.43 p=0.907, ON share 18.4% < 25%, OFF > ON in both halves, q+ 0.077, n_ON 42), V5-4 fails 11 of 15 (ON-OFF -0.03 p=0.581, ON share 18.4%, q+ 0.200, n_ON 258 < 600, C1 +0.01 < 0.15 haircut), V5-5 fails 13 of 16 (lower CI -0.96, ON-OFF -0.27 p=0.832, Spearman rho 0.013 p=0.469, q+ 0.158). The unconditional cells V5-1/V5-2 also fail every substantive gate (lower CI < 0 in the confirmatory window and, as already known, in the 2014-09..2019-12 half; both confirmatory halves < 0; winsor/trim < 0). (3) The partial-run AMBER clause (1,225 < 1,500 files) does not rescue the verdict: RED takes precedence when a kill rule fires, and the 1,225-name panel is effectively the complete 2004-2013 universe reachable from the 2026 list (every name Yahoo served after two throttle-safe passes; names listed after 2014 cannot have this history), so the pre-declared completed-download re-run cannot change the outcome. (4) GREEN was in any case unavailable because V5-8 Part A is unrun and the run is partial. Registered consequence of RED: log and stop; the fresh-start search has exhausted intraday, multi-day and overnight continuation in this data; no live service is written. The result is decisive in the registration's own terms ("a pass there is necessary, not sufficient; a fail is decisive") because the 2004-2013 survivor universe is the window most biased in the rule's favour, and the effect is still significantly negative.

b1_window_sensitivity: Primary B1 window = the executor's [T-64, T-2] (63 event-days whose T+1 open is <= T-1); verifier variant [T-63, T-2] (62 event-days). Day-state agreement between the two on 2004-2013: 98.97% (ON share 0.184 vs 0.187 of all confirmatory days; 0.216 of days on which B1 is defined, from 2005-06-21; 63-day window used on 60.9% of days, 126-day fallback on 24.4%, undefined/OFF 14.7%). V5-3: primary n_ON=42, mean -0.72 [-1.29, -0.24], q+ 0.077, ON-OFF -0.43 p=0.907, OFF -0.29 [-0.61]; variant n_ON=45, mean -0.82 [-1.36, -0.35], q+ 0.077, ON-OFF -0.56 p=0.970, OFF -0.26 [-0.57]. V5-4: primary n_ON=258, mean -0.24 [-0.53, +0.08], q+ 0.200, ON-OFF -0.03 p=0.581, OFF -0.20 [-0.40]; variant n_ON=256, mean -0.32 [-0.63, -0.01], q+ 0.200, ON-OFF -0.14 p=0.779, OFF -0.18 [-0.37]. Unlike the seen window, where the one-day shift moved the quarters-positive flag across the 0.60 line, here it changes nothing: quarters-positive shares are identical, all statistics move slightly further negative, and no gate or verdict changes. The larger structural finding is that B1 was OFF on 82% of confirmatory days because the trailing E2 population mean was negative almost throughout 2005-2013, so the gate is non-discriminating by construction on this window (ON share < 25% gate fails) and the few ON nights were worse than the OFF nights.
per_capital: K=5, E1 first then E2 by day return, net of tier costs, idle nights = 0, confirmatory calendar 2004-01-02..2013-12-31 (2,517 days). V5-1 (E1, 205 trades / 176 nights): 20% each total -14.0%, MDD -14.6%, years>0 1/10 (only 2007 +2.7%); v5 weights 7.5%/3.75% ATR-capped total -5.4%, MDD -5.7%. V5-2 (E2, 1,208 filled of 1,243 / 792 nights): 20% each total -46.8%, MDD -46.8%, years>0 1/10 (2008 -15.4%, every year 2005-2013 negative except 2007 -1.5% raw / +0.1% excess); v5 weights total -13.7%, MDD -13.7%, years>0 2/10. V5-3 (E1|B1 ON, 42 trades): 20% total -6.8%, MDD -7.3%; v5 total -2.3%. V5-4 (E2|B1 ON, 255 trades): 20% total -21.3%, MDD -21.6%, years>0 0/10 (2009 -10.4%); v5 total -5.2%. V5-5 (E1|B2 ON, 88 trades): 20% total -8.5%, MDD -9.3%, years>0 0/10; v5 total -3.2%. Capacity never binds: E1 max 4 per night, 0% unfilled; E2 mean 1.57 / max 16 per night, > 5 on 1.1% of nights, 2.8% unfilled. Full table incl. yearly raw and SPY-excess series: EXEC_v5_confirmatory_percapital.csv.
caveats: Partial-universe label: 1,225 files < the registration's 1,500 threshold, but the frozen list is every symbol of the 2026 list that Yahoo served for 2004-2013 (identical to the pre-check list), i.e. effectively the complete reachable universe; the pre-declared completed-download re-run would add nothing material and cannot change a RED that rests on negative point estimates and a fired kill rule.

Survivorship: the universe is 2026 survivors that already existed and were liquid in 2014; delistings, bankruptcies and acquisition targets of 2004-2013 are absent and later winners are over-represented. For a long continuation leg this biases results IN the rule's favour (registration: the 2004-2013 window is the most biased in the rule's favour; a fail is decisive). The effect is nonetheless significantly negative, and C1 (same-survivor controls) confirms the event names underperform even matched survivors (C1 excess -0.25 E1 / -0.06 E2).

Eligible universe is small: 147-293 names per day (the $50M ADV20$ floor applied to adjusted prices among 1,225 survivors), so E1 n=205 < 300 and V5-3/V5-5 n_ON=42/88. The verdict does not rest on power: four of five family cells have upper CI < 0 (V5-4 upper +0.08), K1 fires on point estimates, and both halves are negative for every cell.

Prices are yfinance split/dividend-adjusted: the $5 prev-close floor acts on adjusted prices and excludes names with large later splits from early years (e.g. AAPL at ~$0.38 adjusted in 2004); this works against the rule (big future winners drop out). ADV$ = adjusted close x split-adjusted volume, approximately split-invariant. SPY file is unadjusted; only ex-dividend overnight legs are affected, negligibly.
2004 contributes no events (the >= 250-row history filter first clears 2004-12-30, exactly as 2014-09..12 had none on the seen window); the effective event window is 2005-01..2013-12.

B1 gate: ON on only 18.4% of confirmatory days (fails the 25-75% discrimination gate) because the trailing E2 population mean was negative almost throughout; B1 defined from 2005-06-21 (undefined = OFF). The verifier-flagged one-day window shift ([T-63,T-2]) changes n_ON by +-3, moves every gated statistic slightly further negative, and changes no gate or verdict; quarters-positive shares are identical (0.077 / 0.200).

B2 defined only from 2007-01-31 (needs 21 + 504 days of dispersion); ON share 31.2% of all days / 45.1% of defined days; Spearman(dispersion, quarterly E2 mean) rho = 0.013, p = 0.469 on 36 quarters -- the seen-window rho of +0.36 does not replicate.
C2 coverage 26.8% overall; for E1 cells C2 exists for only 3 (V5-1), 2 (V5-3) and 1 (V5-5) events, so the C2 > 0 gate is uninformative for E1 (it is not the reason any cell fails).

V5-2's placebo gate (|mean| < 0.20 and not significant) is 'not met' because the Close_T+5 -> Open_T+6 placebo is significantly NEGATIVE (-0.17 [-0.36, -0.01] vs C1), not positive; K3 requires a positive placebo and does not fire.

K4 (survivorship signature) does not fire: for V5-2 the >= $500M tier is the only positive slice (+0.98, n=99) while the $50-100M tier (-0.37) and least-liquid tercile (-0.46) are negative -- the opposite of the survivorship signature; V5-1 is negative in every tier and tercile.
Earnings coverage of 2004-2013 E1 events 28.8% (< 60%, checked before the run): V5-7c stays descriptive (E1 earnings n=40 -0.61 vs non-earnings n=19 -0.99), Holm m = 5 as logged.
V5-7e SPY <= -3% nights: E1 n=0, E2 n=3 -- the risk rule is untestable here. macro_eve uses the NFP first-Friday proxy (BLS calendar not on disk).
V5-8 Part A (15:44 proxy fidelity) was not run; it is moot under RED and would in any case have blocked GREEN.

Decision-tree precedence when clauses overlap was set to RED > AMBER > GREEN (stricter reading); a literal reading of the AMBER partial-run clause would say 'shadow only, no capital, re-decide on completion', which changes nothing operationally because no capital is deployed either way and the completed-download re-run cannot alter the result.

Stricter readings documented in the report: C2 > 0 and winsor/trim > 0 applied to every trading cell; 'OFF <= ON in both halves' applied to V5-5 as well; placebo/mirror gates inherited from V5-1 (E2 cells also from V5-2); liquidity gate on the cell's own subset and on V5-1 for gated cells; missing values fail a gate; K1 'best cell' = family cell with the highest confirmatory mean (V5-2); panel reindexed to the SPY calendar so T+1 is always the next SPY trading day (0 SPY days were absent).

Post-run cosmetic fix only: the yearly CSV/report block was re-sorted by year (2004 had sorted last after the concat) by re-reading the written CSV; no return was recomputed and the script was not re-run. The first invocation failed at parse time (SyntaxError before any computation), so exactly one confirmatory computation occurred.

things_tried.csv: 11 rows appended (5 family cells, 2 B1 sensitivity rows, V5-6, M1, DECISION, and '2004-2013 window status = SEEN'); any further rule test on 2004-2013 joins the Holm family retroactively or voids every v5 verdict.
